doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

title: Union membership and working outside the union
summary: Luthjen's was an open-shop job; De De says he left the union after a month because the officers took the best jobs, and he did better on his own.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: That always was a non-union job. Always was.
Always open shop.
In the old days when you played in the bands around, did they have a union much? No, no, no, no.

Did you ever belong to the union? I did at one time and I didn't stay there but a month. And got out of it. I mean at that time. Yeah. Because it looked like all the big shots were running it, you understand, they were getting all the way. That's my sister Sadie. That's her papa when she was in New York.
Oh yeah, that's nice.
I got out and got for myself then, you see. I mean at that time it didn't do me no good.
Is Sadie still playing the piano at all? Right.
That's right. She said she was just playing for her and her husband.
Really didn't?

Because all in the long of all. Because all in the long of all. The secretary and the president and the walking delegates and all. That's all my dad and older sister. They were getting all the best part of the job. And they sent me all the hours with your house and that was all. You understand what I mean? Sure.
That's the best part of my sister's house in Florida.
That's a friend of mine.

She and I used to go to school and that's her husband. To my estimation I did better out of it. Yeah. That's right, I did. Well now I believe in all I do. I'm not against that, no. I'm not against it but I mean. That's my niece. That's Margaret. He plays piano.
Myself, that's what I'm saying. Yeah.
That's right.
That's right. I quit the union with something. Yes. Healing up the gangs together, well. Yes. He's a good guy. I'm a good guy. I'm a good guy.
I'm a good guy.
I'm a good guy. I'm a good guy. That's right.
That's right.
I quit the union with something.
Yes.
Healing up the gangs together, well. That's just their business. I'm just saying, I got more work outside of it. I do as I please.
